evidence: Caes. B.G. 1.41: mīrum in modum conversae sunt omnium mentēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. mīrus)
terms.comment: Literally “in a wonderful way”; it goes with a verb or an adjective. The comic poets have mīrīs modīs (Plaut., Ter.).

evidence: Liv. 2.1: id mīrum quantum prōfuit ad concordiam cīvitātis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Used as a single adverb, with the indicative: mīrum quantum “surprisingly much”.

evidence: Nep. Milt. 2.5: etsī praeter opīniōnem rēs ceciderat (Lewis & Short, s.v. opīniō)
Cic. de Or. 2.284: praeter exspectātiōnem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: When the surprise is that things went against what was expected; also contrā opīniōnem and praeter exspectātiōnem. With a comparative, opīniōne alone: opīniōne citius, “sooner than expected” (Varro) (see surprise-unexpected-thing).

phrases.latin: id mīrum quantum prōfuit ad concordiam cīvitātis
phrases.english: it did surprisingly much for harmony in the state
